segments.arabic: [364] حدثنا يعقوب بن إبراهيم قال: حدثنا إسماعيل بن علية قال: حدثنا عبد العزيز بن صهيب عن أنس
segments.english: Ya‘qub ibn Ibrahim related to us. He said: Isma‘il ibn ‘Ulayyah related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn Suhayb related to us, from Anas:

segments.arabic: أن رسول الله ﷺ غزا خيبر فصلينا عندها صلاة الغداة بغلس فركب نبي الله ﷺ وركب أبو طلحة وأنا رديف أبي طلحة فأجرى نبي الله ﷺ في زقاق خيبر وإن ركبتي لتمس فخذ نبي الله ﷺ ثم حسر الإزار عن فخذه حتى إني أنظر إلى بياض فخذ نبي الله ﷺ فلما دخل القرية قال الله أكبر خربت خيبر إنا إذا نزلنا بساحة قوم { فساء صباح المنذرين } قالها ثلاثا
segments.english: That the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, attacked Khaybar. We prayed the dawn prayer near it in the darkness before daybreak. The Prophet of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, mounted, and Abu Talhah mounted, with me riding behind Abu Talhah. The Prophet of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, rode swiftly through an alley of Khaybar, and my knee was touching the thigh of the Prophet of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Then he drew the izar away from his thigh, until I could see the whiteness of the thigh of the Prophet of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. When he entered the town, he said: “Allah is greater! Khaybar is ruined! When we descend into a people’s courtyard, then evil is the morning of those who were warned.” He said it three times.

segments.arabic: قال وخرج القوم إلى أعمالهم فقالوا محمد قال عبد العزيز، وقال بعض أصحابنا والخميس يعني الجيش
segments.english: He said: The people came out to their work and said: “Muhammad!” ‘Abd al-‘Aziz said: And some of our companions said: “And the khamis”—meaning the army.

segments.arabic: قال: فأصبناها عنوة فجمع السبي فجاء دحية، فقال: يا نبي الله أعطني جارية من السبي قال اذهب فخذ جارية فأخذ صفية بنت حيي فجاء رجل إلى النبي ﷺ، فقال: يا نبي الله أعطيت دحية صفية بنت حيي سيدة قريظة والنضير لا تصلح إلا لك قال ادعوه بها فجاء بها فلما نظر إليها النبي ﷺ قال: خذ جارية من السبي غيرها قال: فأعتقها النبي ﷺ وتزوجها، فقال له ثابت يا أبا حمزة ما أصدقها قال نفسها أعتقها وتزوجها حتى إذا كان بالطريق جهزتها له أم سليم فأهدتها له من الليل فأصبح النبي ﷺ عروسا، فقال من كان عنده شيء فليجئ به وبسط نطعا فجعل الرجل يجيء بالتمر وجعل الرجل يجيء بالسمن قال وأحسبه قد ذكر السويق قال: فحاسوا حيسا فكانت وليمة رسول الله ﷺ
segments.english: He said: We took it by force. The captives were gathered, and Dihyah came and said: “Prophet of Allah, give me a female captive from among the captives.” He said: “Go and take a female captive.” He took Safiyyah bint Huyayy. A man came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and said: “Prophet of Allah, you have given Dihyah Safiyyah bint Huyayy, the leading lady of Qurayzah and al-Nadir. She is fit only for you.” He said: “Call him with her.” He brought her, and when the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, looked at her, he said: “Take a female captive from among the captives other than her.” He said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, freed her and married her. Thabit said to him: “Abu Hamzah, what did he give her as her marriage payment?” He said: “Herself. He freed her and married her.” When he was on the journey, Umm Sulaym prepared her for him and brought her to him during the night. In the morning the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was a bridegroom. He said: “Whoever has anything, let him bring it.” He spread out a leather sheet. One man would bring dates, and another would bring ghee. He said: I think he also mentioned sawiq. He said: They mixed a hays, and that was the wedding feast of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

notes: The active حسر (he drew away) remains; it is not replaced by the passive became uncovered found in other recensions. Fath al-Bari records the variants. The complete chain, riding behind Abu Talhah, all repeated honorifics, threefold statement, Abd al-Aziz interjection, capture by force and complete marriage and feast account remain. The Quranic phrase within the report corresponds to 37:177; no surrounding verse or commentary is inserted.

Khamis is retained with the source’s own meaning the army. Safiyyah’s identity, the instruction to Dihyah and Thabit’s question to Abu Hamzah remain. نفسها is provisionally Herself, followed by the source’s own explanation of freeing and marrying; it is not silently replaced by an explanatory quotation. Sawiq (a preparation of ground roasted grain) and hays (a mixed food) remain source terms. The uncertainty about sawiq remains. No curd or other recipe ingredient from commentary is inserted.

segments.arabic: [365] حدثنا أبو اليمان قال: أخبرنا شعيب عن الزهري قال: أخبرني عروة أن عائشة قالت
segments.english: Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: ‘Urwah informed me that ‘A’ishah said:

segments.arabic: لقد كان رسول الله ﷺ يصلي الفجر فيشهد معه نساء من المؤمنات متلفعات في مروطهن ثم يرجعن إلى بيوتهن ما يعرفهن أحد
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray Fajr, and some believing women would attend with him, wrapped in their cloaks. Then they would return to their homes, and no one would recognize them.

notes: The complete Abu al-Yaman / Shuayb / al-Zuhri / Urwah / Aishah chain remains. Cloaks provisionally renders murut. The selected report does not say that darkness caused the women not to be recognized; that explanation from other versions is not inserted. The chapter heading has من الثياب in the selected source and في الثياب in the modern print; the selected heading is unchanged.

segments.arabic: [366] حدثنا أحمد بن يونس قال: حدثنا إبراهيم بن سعد قال: حدثنا ابن شهاب عن عروة عن عائشة
segments.english: Ahmad ibn Yunus related to us. He said: Ibrahim ibn Sa‘d related to us. He said: Ibn Shihab related to us, from ‘Urwah, from ‘A’ishah:

segments.arabic: أن النبي ﷺ صلى في خميصة لها أعلام فنظر إلى أعلامها نظرة فلما انصرف قال اذهبوا بخميصتي هذه إلى أبي جهم وأتوني بأنبجانية أبي جهم فإنها ألهتني آنفا عن صلاتي،
segments.english: That the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed in a khamisah with markings. He glanced once at its markings. When he finished, he said: “Take this khamisah of mine to Abu Jahm and bring me Abu Jahm’s anbijaniyyah, for it distracted me just now from my prayer.”

segments.arabic: وقال هشام بن عروة عن أبيه عن عائشة قال النبي ﷺ
segments.english: And Hisham ibn ‘Urwah said, from his father, from ‘A’ishah: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: كنت أنظر إلى علمها وأنا في الصلاة فأخاف أن تفتنني
segments.english: “I was looking at its marking while I was praying, and I fear that it may distract me.”

comparisons.note: The selected Arabic report has two transmissions in one numbered entry. The pinned English comparison numbers their bodies separately as 369 and 370; both were individually inspected, with full selected chains retained.

notes: This is one selected Arabic numbered entry with a later Hisham ibn Urwah / his father / Aishah transmission. Bewley includes both statements under 366; the pinned Khan-family EPUB numbers them separately as 1.8.369 and 1.8.370. Both comparison bodies were inspected and their exact segment coverage is recorded; neither part is dropped or turned into an extra reader entry.

Khamisah is a marked or patterned wrap; anbijaniyyah is an unmarked heavy woollen wrap. Source terms remain instead of importing the English comparison’s long shirt. The single glance, just now and present fear remain. The historical print has حدثني at Ibn Shihab where the selected and modern print have حدثنا; the selected chain is unchanged. Fath al-Bari discusses the wording and garment terms; its interpretation is not added to the report.

segments.arabic: [367] حدثنا أبو معمر عبد الله بن عمرو قال: حدثنا عبد الوارث قال: حدثنا عبد العزيز بن صهيب عن أنس
segments.english: Abu Ma‘mar ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Amr related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Warith related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn Suhayb related to us, from Anas:

segments.arabic: كان قرام لعائشة سترت به جانب بيتها، فقال النبي ﷺ أميطي عنا قرامك هذا فإنه لا تزال تصاويره تعرض في صلاتي
segments.english: ‘A’ishah had a curtain with which she screened a side of her house. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Take this curtain of yours away from us, for its pictures keep appearing before me in my prayer.”

notes: Qiram is rendered curtain; Fath al-Bari describes the thin patterned fabric. The selected text says that Aishah screened the side of her house; the matched Khan-family text says he. The selected female subject remains. No inferred type of picture or legal answer to the chapter question is inserted. The complete Abu Mamar Abd Allah ibn Amr chain remains.

segments.arabic: [368] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: حدثنا الليث عن يزيد عن أبي الخير عن عقبة بن عامر قال
segments.english: ‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Al-Layth related to us, from Yazid, from Abu al-Khayr, from ‘Uqbah ibn ‘Amir, who said:

segments.arabic: أهدي إلي النبي ﷺ فروج حرير فلبسه فصلى فيه ثم انصرف فنزعه نزعا شديدا كالكاره له، وقال لا ينبغي هذا للمتقين
segments.english: A silk farruj was given to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He put it on and prayed in it. Then, when he finished, he pulled it off forcefully, as though disliking it, and said: “This is not fitting for the God-fearing.”

notes: Farruj remains the source garment term: Fath al-Bari describes a coat split at the back. The unnamed giver remains unnamed. The wearing, prayer, forceful removal, apparent dislike and final statement all remain, without an explanation for the removal imported from another account. Both printed witnesses retain the full report.

segments.arabic: [369] حدثنا محمد بن عرعرة قال: حدثني عمر بن أبي زائدة عن عون بن أبي جحيفة عن أبيه قال:
segments.english: Muhammad ibn ‘Ar‘arah related to us. He said: ‘Umar ibn Abi Za’idah related to me, from ‘Awn ibn Abi Juhayfah, from his father, who said:

segments.arabic: رأيت رسول الله ﷺ في قبة حمراء من آدم ورأيت بلالا أخذ وضوء رسول الله ﷺ ورأيت الناس يبتدرون ذاك الوضوء فمن أصاب منه شيئا تمسح به ومن لم يصب منه شيئا أخذ من بلل يد صاحبه ثم رأيت بلالا أخذ عنزة فركزها وخرج النبي ﷺ في حلة حمراء مشمرا صلى إلى العنزة بالناس ركعتين ورأيت الناس والدواب يمرون من بين يدي العنزة
segments.english: I saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in a red leather tent. I saw Bilal take the ablution water of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and I saw the people rushing for that water. Whoever obtained some wiped himself with it, and whoever did not obtain any took some of the moisture from his companion’s hand. Then I saw Bilal take a short spear and plant it. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came out in a red outfit, with his garment tucked up, and led the people in two rak‘ahs facing the spear. I saw people and animals passing in front of the spear.

notes: The complete chain is Awn ibn Abi Juhayfah from his father. The Bewley introductory line shortens this differently; it does not replace the selected chain. The two rakahs, absent from that comparison’s body, remain.

Ablution water retains the source’s wording without adding used or left over. The garment being tucked up is retained without adding visible feet or sleeves. The people and animals pass in front of the spear; no wording is added that puts them between the worshipper and the spear. Both printed witnesses retain the full sequence.

segments.arabic: [370] حدثنا علي بن عبد الله قال: حدثنا سفيان قال: حدثنا أبو حازم قال
segments.english: ‘Ali ibn ‘Abd Allah related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us. He said: Abu Hazim related to us. He said:

segments.arabic: سألوا سهل بن سعد من أي شيء المنبر، فقال: ما بقي بالناس أعلم مني هو من أثل الغابة عمله فلان مولى فلانة لرسول الله ﷺ وقام عليه رسول الله ﷺ حين عمل ووضع فاستقبل القبلة كبر وقام الناس خلفه فقرأ وركع وركع الناس خلفه ثم رفع رأسه ثم رجع القهقري فسجد على الأرض ثم عاد إلى المنبر ثم ركع ثم رفع رأسه ثم رجع القهقري حتى سجد بالأرض فهذا شأنه
segments.english: They asked Sahl ibn Sa‘d what the pulpit was made of. He said: “There is no one left among the people who knows more about it than I do. It is made of tamarisk from al-Ghabah. So-and-so, the mawla of such-and-such a woman, made it for the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood on it when it had been made and set in place. He faced the qiblah and said ‘Allah is greater,’ and the people stood behind him. He recited and bowed, and the people bowed behind him. Then he raised his head, stepped backwards and prostrated on the ground. Then he returned to the pulpit, bowed and raised his head. Then he stepped backwards until he prostrated on the ground. That was what he did.”

segments.arabic: قال أبو عبد الله قال علي بن عبد الله سألني أحمد بن حنبل رحمه الله عن هذا الحديث قال: فإنما أردت أن النبي ﷺ كان أعلى من الناس فلا بأس أن يكون الإمام أعلى من الناس بهذا الحديث قال: فقلت: إن سفيان بن عيينة كان يسأل عن هذا كثيرا فلم تسمعه منه قال لا
segments.english: Abu ‘Abd Allah said: ‘Ali ibn ‘Abd Allah said: Ahmad ibn Hanbal, may Allah have mercy on him, asked me about this hadith. He said: “I only meant that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was higher than the people. So, according to this hadith, there is no harm in the imam being higher than the people.” He said: I said: “Sufyan ibn ‘Uyaynah used to be asked about this often. Did you not hear it from him?” He said: “No.”

notes: The pulpit is of tamarisk from al-Ghabah. The unknown maker and woman remain unnamed. Mawla is retained rather than choosing an unexpressed legal relationship. Stepping backwards is explicit. The historical print and Khan-family comparison include a second recitation; the selected and modern print do not, so none is inserted.

The closing Abu Abd Allah / Ali ibn Abd Allah / Ahmad ibn Hanbal discussion is a visible Transmission note, not Prophetic speech. The source’s mercy honorific and final question to Ahmad about hearing from Sufyan, with his answer No, remain. The matched Khan-family body abridges this discussion; Bewley also omits the compiler attribution and mercy honorific. The selected pronoun He said is not silently replaced with a stronger identification of the speaker. Fath al-Bari discusses the exchange separately.

segments.arabic: [371] حدثنا محمد بن عبد الرحيم قال: حدثنا يزيد بن هارون قال: أخبرنا حميد الطويل عن أنس بن مالك
segments.english: Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Rahim related to us. He said: Yazid ibn Harun related to us. He said: Humayd al-Tawil informed us, from Anas ibn Malik:

segments.arabic: أن رسول الله ﷺ سقط عن فرسه فجحشت ساقه أو كتفه وآلى من نسائه شهرا فجلس في مشربة له درجتها من جذوع فأتاه أصحابه يعودونه فصلى بهم جالسا وهم قيام فلما سلم قال إنما جعل الإمام ليؤتم به فإذا كبر فكبروا وإذا ركع فاركعوا وإذا سجد فاسجدوا وإن صلى قائما فصلوا قياما ونزل لتسع وعشرين فقالوا يا رسول الله إنك آليت شهرا، فقال إن الشهر تسع وعشرون
segments.english: That the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, fell from his horse and his lower leg or shoulder was grazed. He swore to stay away from his wives for a month and stayed in an upper room of his whose steps were made of tree trunks. His companions came to visit him. He led them in prayer while sitting, and they were standing. When he gave the salutation, he said: “The imam is appointed only to be followed. When he says ‘Allah is greater,’ say ‘Allah is greater’; when he bows, bow; when he prostrates, prostrate; and if he prays standing, pray standing.” He came down after twenty-nine days. They said: “Messenger of Allah, you swore for a month.” He said: “The month is twenty-nine days.”

notes: The uncertainty lower leg or shoulder remains. The selected and modern print say tree trunks; the historical print and English comparisons specify date-palm trunks. No tree species is inserted. The upper room, month-long oath, visit, seated imam with standing companions, every instruction and twenty-nine-day reply remain.

This selected report ends its posture instructions with praying standing. The instruction to pray seated that appears in other versions is not imported. No additional legal ruling about the oath or posture is appended.

segments.arabic: [372] حدثنا مسدد عن خالد قال: حدثنا سليمان الشيباني عن عبد الله بن شداد عن ميمونة قالت
segments.english: Musaddad related to us, from Khalid, who said: Sulayman al-Shaybani related to us, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Shaddad, from Maymunah, who said:

segments.arabic: كان رسول الله ﷺ يصلي وأنا حذاءه وأنا حائض وربما أصابني ثوبه إذا سجد قالت وكان يصلي على الخمرة
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray with me beside him while I was menstruating. Sometimes his garment touched me when he prostrated. She said: He used to pray on a khumrah.

notes: The complete chain through Khalid and Sulayman al-Shaybani remains. Maymunah is beside him and menstruating; the selected report does not add that she is sitting. Her closing She said statement remains. Khumrah is a small prayer mat, distinguished from the larger hasir of the next chapter; the explanatory description stays outside the quotation.

segments.arabic: [373] حدثنا عبد الله قال: أخبرنا مالك عن إسحاق بن عبد الله بن أبي طلحة عن أنس بن مالك
segments.english: ‘Abd Allah related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Ishaq ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn Abi Talhah, from Anas ibn Malik:

segments.arabic: أن جدته مليكة دعت رسول الله ﷺ لطعام صنعته له فأكل منه، ثم قال قوموا فلأصل لكم قال أنس فقمت إلى حصير لنا قد اسود من طول ما لبس فنضحته بماء فقام رسول الله ﷺ وصففت أنا واليتيم وراءه والعجوز من ورائنا فصلى لنا رسول الله ﷺ ركعتين ثم انصرف
segments.english: That his grandmother Mulaykah invited the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, to some food she had prepared for him. He ate some of it, then said: “Get up, so that I may pray for you.” Anas said: I went to a mat of ours that had become black from long use and sprinkled it with water. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood, and the orphan and I stood in a row behind him, with the old woman behind us. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, led us in two rak‘ahs, then left.

notes: The source’s initial Abd Allah remains unexpanded; the historical print adds ibn Yusuf. The pronoun his grandmother is retained because Fath al-Bari records different identifications of its referent, Anas or Ishaq. No determination is silently inserted. The historical print adds an honorific after Mulaykah which is absent in the selected and modern text; none is added.

The source says our mat and sprinkled it, not my mat and washed it as in the Khan-family comparison. The orphan and old woman remain unnamed, and no ablution or reason for sprinkling is imported from commentary. The complete invitation, meal, arrangement, two rakahs and departure remain.

segments.arabic: [374] حدثنا أبو الوليد قال: حدثنا شعبة قال: حدثنا سليمان الشيباني عن عبد الله بن شداد عن ميمونة قالت
segments.english: Abu al-Walid related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us. He said: Sulayman al-Shaybani related to us, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Shaddad, from Maymunah, who said:

segments.arabic: كان النبي ﷺ يصلي على الخمرة
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray on a khumrah.

notes: The complete Abu al-Walid / Shubah / Sulayman al-Shaybani / Abd Allah ibn Shaddad / Maymunah chain remains. The selected and modern text say Prophet; the historical print says Messenger of Allah. The selected wording is unchanged. Khumrah remains the source term for the small mat.

segments.arabic: [375] حدثنا إسماعيل قال: حدثني مالك عن أبي النضر مولى عمر بن عبيد الله عن أبي سلمة بن عبد الرحمن عن عائشة زوج النبي ﷺ أنها قالت
segments.english: Isma‘il related to us. He said: Malik related to me, from Abu al-Nadr, the mawla of ‘Umar ibn ‘Ubayd Allah, from Abu Salamah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman, from ‘A’ishah, the wife of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

segments.arabic: كنت أنام بين يدي رسول الله ﷺ ورجلاي في قبلته فإذا سجد غمزني فقبضت رجلي فإذا قام بسطتهما قالت والبيوت يومئذ ليس فيها مصابيح
segments.english: I used to sleep in front of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, with my legs in the direction of his qiblah. When he prostrated, he nudged me and I drew my legs in. When he stood, I stretched them out. She said: The houses in those days had no lamps.

notes: The full Abu al-Nadr mawla relationship and Aishah’s description as the Prophet’s wife, with its honorific, remain in the chain. The source says he nudged me; the Khan-family comparison specifies her legs. No body part is added to the action. Both drawing in and stretching out the legs remain, followed by her statement that the houses had no lamps.

segments.arabic: [376] حدثنا يحيى بن بكير قال: حدثنا الليث عن عقيل عن ابن شهاب قال: أخبرني عروة أن عائشة أخبرته
segments.english: Yahya ibn Bukayr related to us. He said: Al-Layth related to us, from ‘Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, who said: ‘Urwah informed me that ‘A’ishah informed him:

segments.arabic: أن رسول الله ﷺ كان يصلي وهي بينه وبين القبلة على فراش أهله اعتراض الجنازة
segments.english: That the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray while she was between him and the qiblah on his family’s bed, lying crosswise like a body laid out for a funeral.

notes: The report remains in the third person after Aishah informed Urwah; it is not converted to a first-person quotation as in the Khan-family comparison. The family bed, her position between him and the qiblah, and the comparison to a body laid out for a funeral remain. This describes the crosswise position, without adding a claim that she was dead. Both Arabic prints preserve the comparison.

segments.arabic: [377] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: حدثنا الليث عن يزيد عن عراك عن عروة
segments.english: ‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Al-Layth related to us, from Yazid, from ‘Irak, from ‘Urwah:

segments.arabic: أن النبي ﷺ كان يصلي وعائشة معترضة بينه وبين القبلة على الفراش الذي ينامان عليه
segments.english: That the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray with ‘A’ishah lying crosswise between him and the qiblah on the bed on which they both slept.

notes: The selected chain ends with Urwah directly reporting the Prophet’s action. Aishah is named in the body, not added as an extra link in the chain from the preceding report. Both printed witnesses preserve this structure and the shared bed on which they both slept.
